 Learn more McGrath RentCorp (MGRC) just released third quarter 2026 results, reporting higher sales, revenue, net income, and earnings per share compared with the same period last year, giving investors fresh numbers to reassess the stock. 
 That set of results has landed alongside a strong run in the shares, with McGrath RentCorp's 1 month share price return of 10.11% and year to date share price gain of 23.01% indicating building momentum around the story. 
 Scan beyond McGrath RentCorp and see how its third quarter momentum compares with a curated 33 high quality undervalued stocks that pair strong fundamentals with potential mispricing. 
 After a move like this and fresh quarterly figures on the table, the real issue is simple: Does McGrath RentCorp still offer an attractive trade off between upside and risk at today's price, based on its valuation? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 11% Undervalued 
 McGrath RentCorp's most followed narrative points to a fair value of $145.40, compared with the last close at $129.44. This puts the spotlight firmly on whether the current price reflects its rental growth plans, capital spending, and segment mix. 
 Ongoing Mobile Modular geographic expansion and the build out of add on services such as Mobile Modular Plus and site related work, reflected in 11% bookings growth and higher revenue per unit in Q2 2026, can continue to shift McGrath RentCorp's mix toward higher value rental projects that support revenue and margin growth. 
 See why 2 investors see McGrath RentCorp as 11% undervalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $145.40 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the thesis around McGrath RentCorp can be knocked off course if weak Portable Storage utilization persists or if Enviroplex's recent EBITDA loss drags on group returns. 
 Find out about the key risks to this McGrath RentCorp narrative . 
 Another View: McGrath RentCorp Through The Earnings Lens 
 Analysts see McGrath RentCorp as attractively priced using their fair value of $145.40, yet the current P/E of 19.8x sits above a fair ratio of 16.4x and well below peers at 41.3x. That mix of discount to industry but premium to fair ratio raises a simple question for you: Is the margin of safety big enough?
